questions.prompt: What does the execute bit (x) mean on a directory?
choices: The directory is a runnable program
You may enter the directory and resolve names inside it
Anyone may delete files in the directory
The directory will be searched by locate
questions.why: On a directory, x is traverse: you can cd into it and look up names. chmod 777 is not a fix; it gives every account write access.

questions.prompt: systemctl enable nginx does which of these?
choices: Marks the unit to start on boot; it may still be stopped or failed
Reloads nginx after a config change
questions.why: enable ≠ start. A unit can be enabled and still failed. Read systemctl status and the journal before editing the unit file.

questions.prompt: You kill the PID of a process that systemd is managing with Restart=always. What usually happens?
choices: The service stays down until you enable it again
systemd starts a new process for that unit
questions.why: Killing a process is not the same as stopping a systemd service. If Restart= is set, systemd brings it back. Use systemctl stop.

questions.prompt: On modern Ubuntu, which command lists listening TCP/UDP sockets without DNS lookups?
questions.why: ss replaced netstat on modern Ubuntu. -tuln is TCP/UDP, listening, numeric. If ss is missing, install iproute2.

questions.prompt: journalctl prints nothing after a reboot. The most likely cause is:
choices: journald is storing only in memory under /run/log/journal
questions.why: An empty journal after reboot often means Storage is volatile. That is a persistence setting, not “Linux has no logs.”
127.0.0.1 is this host. A process listening only on 127.0.0.1 is not reachable from another machine.

questions.prompt: df -h shows 100% on /. What should you do first?
choices: Find the full mount with df, then du, and free space before anything else
questions.why: Nothing else works well on a full root filesystem. Identify the mount, find large directories, rotate or delete logs. Do not reboot and hope.
